title: Achromatism and Its Applications
notes: **Achromatic combination:** a convex crown-glass lens paired with a concave flint-glass lens. The crown lens converges all colours; the flint lens diverges more for violet than for red, canceling chromatic spread.
**Condition for achromatism:** $\omega_1/f_1 + \omega_2/f_2 = 0$. Since $\omega_1$ and $\omega_2$ are both positive, $f_1$ and $f_2$ must have opposite signs: one converging, one diverging.
**Result:** two colours (usually red and blue) are brought to the same focus. Intermediate colours are close enough that the image appears colour-free to the eye.
**Applications:** camera lenses, telescope objectives, microscope objectives all use achromatic doublets or more complex multi-element designs to eliminate chromatic aberration.
**Apochromatic lenses:** advanced designs that bring three colours to the same focus using special glasses with anomalous dispersion.
